voyage.content: Apartment hotel. Fairly far out in northwest Kyoto but the prices are reasonable. Prices are significantly lower for stays of 7 or more nights. Payment by cash only. No daily cleaning and no bath towels provided. Bus journey from Kyoto Station takes about 50 minutes.

voyage.name: GuestHouse Bon
voyage.content: Located in northwest Kyoto, immediately east of Daitokuji. Inexpensive bicycle rentals. The guest house owner has lived in Western countries before and can speak fluent English and a pinch of Spanish. All Japanese-style rooms, but can be converted to dorm style upon request for larger parties.

voyage.name: Momiji-ya
voyage.price: All rooms are designed for at least 2 people. Prices start from ¥14700
voyage.content: Although this hotel operates year round, it is extremely popular in the autumn ("momiji" is the Japanese term for the changing of leaves). It is located in the quiet, far northeastern area of Takao near the foot of the stairway leading to Jingo-ji. It makes for a nice retreat, and you can opt to stay in a room with an open-air bath to relax while you enjoy the natural surroundings.

voyage.name: Grand Prince Hotel Kyoto
voyage.price: Prices vary greatly from ¥11000-45000, depending on the room

voyage.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
voyage.hours: No opening or closing times are listed, but if you arrive before 08:00 you'll beat most of the crowds
voyage.content: Another of Kyoto's jewels, located just south of Higashiyama in the Fushimi area. Dedicated to Inari, the Japanese fox goddess, Fushimi-Inari-taisha is the head shrine (taisha) for 40,000 Inari shrines across Japan. Stretching 230 meters up the hill behind it are hundreds of bright red torii (gates). A visitor could easily spend several hours walking up the hillside, taking in the beautiful views of the city of Kyoto

voyage.name: Fushimi Momoyama Castle
voyage.alt: 桃山城, Momoyama-jō; officially 伏見城, Fushimi-jō
voyage.content: This castle was once a favorite of Toyotomi Hideyoshi. The original was dismantled in 1623, but a 1964 reconstruction went up in its memory with a small museum and gold-lined tea room.

voyage.name: Teradaya
voyage.content: It was here at this inn where Ryōma Sakamoto, a famous samurai who wanted to overthrow the Tokugawa, was injured in an attack, although he escaped. Some pictures, his handgun, and other historical artifacts are viewable inside.

voyage.name: Tōfuku-ji
voyage.content: A large temple complex with many small and beautiful gardens nearby. Hordes of Japanese tourists visit during the fall months, when the leaves show a dazzling array of colors, but it's not as well known to foreigners. A pleasant side path through the woods connects it to the Fushimi Inari grounds. Provides beginner Zen meditation sessions on Sunday mornings.

voyage.name: Jōnan-gū Shrine
voyage.price: Entrance to the shrine grounds is free, but the garden costs ¥500 to enter
voyage.content: Although Jōnan-gū Shrine is rarely visited by foreign tourists, it is a beautiful shrine with extensive history. It was established by Emperor Kammu when Kyoto became the nation's capital. At the end of the Heian period, it became home to retired emperor Goshirakawa. As a result, the beautiful Rakusui-en Garden was constructed. As a former Imperial Villa, Jōnan-gū Shrine is a great alternative for those who are unabl

voyage.name: Daigo-ji
voyage.price: Each part costs ¥600 to enter however discount tickets can be purchased to see two (¥1000) or all three (¥1500)
voyage.hours: The Garan and Sanbōin are open Mar-Nov: daily 09:00-17:00, and Dec-Feb: daily 09:00-16:00. The museum is open daily 09:00-16:00
voyage.content: Daigoji is a large temple complex consisting of the garan (main complex), Sanbōin Garden, and Reihōkan Museum. The size and position of the temple, slightly removed from the city, creates a more peaceful, serene setting. As a registered World Heritage Site, the temple has a lot of history, with the oldest remaining structure being the five-story pagoda built in 951. The Sanbōin is the temple's garden, and despite bei

voyage.name: Zuishin-in
voyage.content: According to legend, this is where Ono no Komachi, one of Japan's famous femme fatales, resided. She made Prince Fukakusa agree to court her for 100 days before she would agree to marry him, but on the 99th day, he died, leaving her single and her beauty to fade.

voyage.name: Kajū-ji
voyage.content: A temple with a peaceful lily pond and a variety of cherry trees.

voyage.name: Nagaoka Tenmangū Shrine
voyage.content: A Shinto shrine in Nagaokakyō, dedicated to Sugawara no Michizane (845–903), the Heian-period scholar and court official who is revered as the deity of learning and scholarship. Michizane is said to have visited the area before his exile to Kyushu, and the shrine was established in his memory. Its grounds include a large pond crossed by a distinctive vermilion bridge and an avenue of kirishima azaleas, which bloom sp

voyage.name: Sennyū-ji Temple
voyage.content: Sennyū-ji Temple is an important Buddhist temple complex in southeastern Kyoto, particularly notable for its close historical association with the Japanese imperial family. Its buildings, imperial tombs and artworks make it a more historically substantial attraction than its relatively quiet setting might suggest.

voyage.name: Oharano Shrine
voyage.content: The shrine is believed to have been moved to Nagaokakyo at the bidding of Empress Kammu, who made it the shrine of the Fujiwara family's guardian god. The Imperial Court made annual offerings at this shrine. The pond within the shrine precincts was once a popular place for writing poetry. The Sengan-zakura tree in the precincts is nicknamed "phantom cherry blossom", because it only blooms for just 2-3 days. Some say

voyage.name: Shōbō-ji
voyage.content: A Shingon sect temple featuring an impressive statue of the 3-faced thousand armed Kannon and a beautiful, well-kept Zen rock garden. Many of the rocks within the garden were chosen to resemble animals, like a rabbit and frog.

voyage.name: Shōji-ji
voyage.content: Nicknamed Cherry Blossom Temple (hana no tera), it hosts a beautiful display of blossoms in the spring.

voyage.name: Yoshimine-dera
voyage.content: In 1034 Emperor Go-Ichijo gave Yoshimine-dera imperial rank, so the head priest was a member of the imperial family for many years, although it is no longer so today. The 20th temple on the Saigoku Kannon Pilgrimage.

voyage.name: JRA Kyoto Racecourse
voyage.content: For those interested in horse races, Kyoto's racecourse is the biggest and most significant in the Kansai area.

voyage.name: Riverboat Cruises
voyage.price: ¥1000 for adults, ¥500 for elementary school and younger
voyage.hours: Call to make a reservation to schedule your ride. No tours are offered on Mondays
voyage.content: A peaceful ride down the canal past all of the historic sake breweries. It's a unique experience that is both scenic and affordable.

voyage.name: Ryomakan
voyage.content: An interesting souvenir shop dedicated to the famous samurai Ryoma Sakamoto. Inside you'll find some of the typical tourist souvenirs, like Ryoma Sakamoto keychains, but there are also some interesting and unique finds. Those looking to purchase swords may find that this shop sells more authentic swords than those in Kyoto's larger tourist spots.

voyage.name: Usagiya
voyage.content: Serves a variety of delicious ramen dishes.

voyage.name: Uosaburo
voyage.content: A pricey restaurant serving local Kyoto cuisine with a variety of set options.

voyage.name: Torisei
voyage.content: Serves a variety of chicken and meat dishes.

voyage.name: Ramen Factory Kyoto
voyage.content: Ramen Factory Kyoto consists of the Ramen Restaurant (for eating - tabemasu) which offers different types of ramen such as Miso, Shoyu (Soy sauce), Shio (Salt) and Ramen Experience (for experience - taiken) which is the only restaurant in Japan where you are able to make original ramen from scratch by your hand and enjoy its deliciousness. Ramen Factory has the root from “Menbakaichidai” which is famous as Fire Ramen

voyage.name: Gekkeikan
voyage.content: Founded in 1637, this local sake brewing company remains popular among Japanese even today. Many of the old breweries still exist and visitors can tour Gekkeikan and visit the attached museum to get a glimpse of how the sake is made.

voyage.name: Hotel Kyoto Eminence
voyage.alt: ホテル京都エミナース eminaasu
voyage.price: Prices start from ¥8750 for hotel rooms. For those who just want to take advantage of the onsen, you can enter for ¥800
voyage.content: A luxury hotel outside of the inner city in the Oharano area. There is an onsen attached, which can be enjoyed with or without hotel reservations.

voyage.name: Urban Hotel Kyoto
voyage.price: Prices start from ¥7000 (single). A nice budget option for two people is the semi-double for ¥9000
voyage.content: A nice hotel in the heart of the Fushimi area, just a 15 minute walk away from Fushimi Inari Taisha.
